# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 3

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 3 — Paths Leading to Sin
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 6

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: "resembles it" vs. "like it"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "everything like it" |
| LOGOS | "everything that resembles it" |
| PNEUMA | "anything that even looks like it" |

**Issue:** ὅμοιον αὐτῷ = "similar/like to it." PNEUMA's emphasis is helpful but interpretive.
**Ruling:** "Everything that resembles it" (LOGOS) adopted. Clear and precise.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: "generated" vs. "begotten"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "murders are begotten" |
| LOGOS | "murders are generated" |
| PNEUMA | "they all breed the same thing" |

**Issue:** γεννῶνται = are born/generated. "Begotten" (EMET) has a theological resonance that may be distracting here. "Generated" is more neutral.
**Ruling:** "Generated" (LOGOS) adopted throughout the causal chain sections.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: "lets his eyes wander" vs. "lifts up his eyes"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "one who lifts up his eyes" |
| LOGOS | "one who lets his eyes wander" |
| PNEUMA | "let your eyes wander where they shouldn't" |

**Issue:** The Greek metaphoroptometer (lifting eyes) is a circumlocution for lustful looking. EMET is more literal; LOGOS and PNEUMA clarify the idiom.
**Ruling:** "One who lets his eyes wander" (LOGOS) adopted. The idiom needs to be understood, and "lifts up his eyes" alone is ambiguous in English.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.4: rendering of divination terms

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "observer of omens / enchanter / astrologer / ritual purifier" |
| LOGOS | "one who looks for omens / enchanter / astrologer / practitioner of purification rites" |
| PNEUMA | "seek out omens / enchanters / astrologers / ritual cleansers" |

**Issue:** Four distinct Greek terms are used. The most disputed is περικαθαίρων: EMET has "ritual purifier," LOGOS "practitioner of purification rites," PNEUMA "ritual cleansers."
**Ruling:** LOGOS adopted. "Practitioner of purification rites" is the most descriptive and accurate for this priestly-magical function.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.8: ἄκακος — "guileless" vs. "innocent"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "guileless" |
| LOGOS | "innocent" |
| PNEUMA | "innocent" |

**Issue:** ἄκακος = without evil/guile. "Guileless" is more precise and distinct from "innocent" (which can imply inexperience or naivety).
**Ruling:** "Guileless" (EMET) adopted. It captures the positive ethical quality of transparent motives, not merely the absence of wrongdoing.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.10: divine providence — word choice

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "nothing happens" (apart from God) |
| LOGOS | "nothing occurs apart from God" |
| PNEUMA | "nothing happens outside of God's hand" |

**Issue:** χωρὶς θεοῦ = without/apart from God. PNEUMA adds "God's hand" which is interpretive but poetic. The Greek has no "hand."
**Ruling:** "Nothing happens apart from God" adopted. Most literal. PNEUMA's addition, while resonant, goes beyond the text.
